title: Schedules and timetables
goal: Read a simple work schedule or class timetable, and say when you work or study: days, hours, breaks, full-time or part-time.

blocks.title: Coffee break in Gatineau
blocks.context: Lucie and Raj compare their schedules.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Tu travailles à temps plein, Raj ?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Oui, je travaille du lundi au vendredi, de huit heures trente à seize heures trente.
lines.en: Yes, I work Monday to Friday, from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Je prends une heure, à midi. Et toi ?
lines.en: I take an hour, at noon. And you?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Moi, je travaille à temps partiel à l'hôpital, le mardi, le jeudi et le samedi. Je commence à sept heures et je finis à quinze heures.
lines.en: I work part-time at the hospital, on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays. I start at 7 a.m. and finish at 3 p.m.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Oui. Mais le dimanche, c'est mon jour de congé ! Et le lundi soir, j'ai mon cours de français, de dix-huit heures à vingt et une heures.
lines.en: Yes. But Sunday is my day off! And on Monday evenings I have my French class, from 6 to 9 p.m.

blocks.title: From… to…
blocks.pattern: du + jour au + jour   •   de + heure à + heure
blocks.note: With days: [[du]] (de + le) and [[au]] (à + le), the same contractions you learned for places in town. With times: just [[de]] and [[à]].

blocks.title: Start and finish
blocks.pattern: commencer à + heure   •   finir à + heure
blocks.note: [[commencer]] is a regular -er verb, but with nous you write **ç**: [[nous commençons]]. [[finir]] is the -ir verb from the last lesson.

examples.fr: Le cours finit à vingt et une heures trente.

blocks.title: Le lundi or lundi?
blocks.body:
A small word makes a big difference:

- [[lundi]] = this Monday, one time: [[Je travaille lundi.]] (I'm working on Monday.)
- [[le lundi]] = every Monday: [[Je travaille le lundi.]] (I work on Mondays.)

Schedules are about habits, so you will see [[le]] a lot: [[le samedi]], [[le mardi et le jeudi]], [[le soir]] (in the evening).

blocks.title: Reading times in a schedule
blocks.body:
Written schedules use the **24-hour clock**, with **h** instead of a colon:

- [[8 h 30]] → *huit heures trente* (8:30 a.m.)
- [[17 h]] → *dix-sept heures* (5 p.m.)
- [[21 h 15]] → *vingt et une heures quinze* (9:15 p.m.)

And two useful words: [[à temps plein]] (full-time) and [[à temps partiel]] (part-time). [[La pause]] is a break; [[un jour de congé]] is a day off.

blocks.title: Schedules, Québec style
blocks.body:
- **L'horaire:** in Québec, your work or class timetable is [[mon horaire]]: [[J'ai un horaire de jour]] (I work days). In France, a personal timetable is more often [[mon emploi du temps]].
- **Le dîner:** in Québec, [[le déjeuner]] is breakfast, [[le dîner]] is lunch and [[le souper]] is supper. So the lunch break is [[la pause du dîner]] (France: [[la pause déjeuner]]).
- **La fin de semaine:** Québec says [[la fin de semaine]]; France says [[le week-end]].
- **Le quart de travail:** a *shift* in a hospital, factory or store is [[un quart]]: [[le quart de soir]], [[le quart de nuit]].
- **Temps plein:** you will see [[poste à temps plein]] or [[emploi à temps partiel]] in job ads. In casual speech you may hear some people drop the [[à]] ([[Je travaille temps plein]]). Just recognize it; say and write [[à temps plein]].

In conversation, people often use the 12-hour clock: [[Je travaille de neuf à cinq]]. Written schedules use the 24-hour clock.

- [[Je commence 9 h]] → [[Je commence à 9 h]]. You need [[à]] before the time.
- [[de le lundi à le vendredi]] → [[du lundi au vendredi]]. Always contract.
- [[en temps plein]] → [[à temps plein]].
- [[Je travaille les lundis]] is possible, but the usual way is [[le lundi]] (singular) for every Monday.
- [[nous commencons]] → [[nous commençons]], with the cedilla.

lines.tip: Glide from du to au without a pause.

In partiel, the t sounds like s: par-siel.

blocks.prompt: Describe your weekly schedule for work or classes: full-time or part-time, which days, what time you start and finish, your break, and your day off.
checklist: à temps plein or à temps partiel
your day off or the weekend

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je travaille à temps plein, du lundi au vendredi. Je commence à huit heures et je finis à seize heures. La pause du dîner est à midi. Le mardi soir, j'ai un cours de français, de dix-huit heures à vingt et une heures. La fin de semaine, je suis en congé !
models.en: I work full-time, Monday to Friday. I start at 8 and I finish at 4 p.m. The lunch break is at noon. On Tuesday evenings, I have a French class from 6 to 9 p.m. On weekends, I'm off!

blocks.prompt: A friend wants to have coffee with you. Write a short message with your schedule this week: when you work or study, and when you are free (libre).
checklist: Give your work or class hours with de… à…
Use le + day for a habit
Say when you are free (je suis libre…)
Ask a question at the end

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Sofia ! Cette semaine, je travaille du lundi au jeudi, de 9 h à 17 h. Le vendredi, j'ai mon cours de francisation de 13 h à 16 h. Je suis libre vendredi soir et samedi. Est-ce que tu es libre samedi matin ?
models.en: Hi Sofia! This week I'm working Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. On Fridays I have my French class from 1 to 4 p.m. I'm free Friday evening and Saturday. Are you free Saturday morning?

summary:
- Say days and hours with [[du lundi au vendredi]] and [[de 9 h à 17 h]]
- Use [[commencer à]] and [[finir à]] + a time, and [[le lundi]] for every Monday
- Read a work schedule or class timetable in the 24-hour clock
- Talk about [[à temps plein]], [[à temps partiel]], [[la pause du dîner]] and [[un jour de congé]]
